changelog:
v1.30.0 - **Root-cause fixes: intermittent "no projectile" + missing-terrain bugs (v1.30.0).** Two long-standing Heisenbugs traced to their actual roots. **(1) Ranged weapons that played their sound + animation but fired NO projectile** (Razzi, Akimbo and others, in bursts right after an enemy died or after the player was hit) were caused by a *freed-object typed assignment*: `WeaponSystem._do_ranged` read the player's locked/hovered enemy straight into a typed `Node3D` target, but when that enemy had just died the reference was already freed, and assigning a freed object into a typed var **throws in Godot 4** -- aborting the shot after the sound/anim but before the spawn loop (no projectile, no muzzle flash, no explosion). The locked/hovered and homing targets are now read into untyped locals and `is_instance_valid()`-guarded before use. **(2) Intermittent missing terrain/obstacles** (blue-grid floor while enemies still spawned) was the **Godot 4.7 global-class registration race**: a script reaching another `class_name`'s *static* members by bare name can fail to resolve when compiled early or on a worker thread. Hardened systemically -- ten pure static-utility scripts (`MapConfig`, `CombatUtils`, `DamageResolver`, `StatusEffects`, `StatusVFX`, `ProjectileVisualBuilder`, `UIStyles`, `StatFormatter`, `KeybindsTabBuilder`, `CelShadingTabBuilder`) dropped `class_name` and are now reached via `const X = preload(...)` in every consumer; type-classes that also expose statics (`Enemy`/`Prop`) route their static reads through differently-named preload-consts (`EnemyClass`/`PropClass`) while keeping `class_name` for casts. **Tooling:** added `tools/run_godot.sh`, a failsafe that refuses to launch a second Godot instance (a concurrent headless `--editor`/`--import` next to an open editor corrupts `.godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg`). All temporary fire-lifecycle diagnostics were removed. **Also in this release:** projectile *homing* is now enabled across 19 weapon / secondary / level-up entries (the steering mechanic already existed in code but had no config to drive it) -- affected shots curve toward the locked/hovered target and re-acquire mid-flight. Verified: clean headless editor compile (zero parse/script errors), a healthy class cache, and the headless regression suites pass.
v1.29.0 - Update bugs.md, balancing.md, and features.md with new translated and polished playtest notes, issues, and requests, including the key bindings bug.
v1.28.0 - **Performance pass — crowd-framerate optimizations (v1.29.0).** A broad pass targeting the framerate drops reported in crowded fights — almost entirely single-threaded CPU work that scales with on-screen entities. **Zero-visual-impact:** off-screen enemies now pause their skeletal `AnimationPlayer` (a `VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D` drives `active`, with a near-player distance safety-net so a visible enemy can never freeze) — the single biggest crowd win; a new `NodePool` recycles the per-hit/per-kill churn (`DamageNumber`, `BloodVFX`, `DeathVFX`, XP/Coin drops) instead of instantiate/`queue_free` per event — this also **fixes a pre-existing leak** where `DeathVFX` never freed itself and accumulated for the whole run; per-enemy weapon-system bookkeeping is strided across frames; `DeathVFX`/`MeleeVFX`/`SprayVFX` stop allocating materials/meshes per use; explosion/impact flash lights gained a global concurrent cap (`FlashLight.can_spawn()`); and `LightingDirector`'s per-frame sun/moon light writes are dirty-checked. **Very-low-impact:** distant on-screen enemies animate at ~1/3 rate (correct speed via manual `advance()`); status-effect particles converted `CPUParticles3D`→`GPUParticles3D`; `DeathVFX`/`FirePool`/`IceTrail`/status particle counts now scale down with the on-screen enemy count (full detail with a few enemies, ~30% floor in a big crowd); SSAO intensity 4→1.5 (no 6.0 cel-mode bump); directional shadow distance 45→25 m; window lights 2-4→1-2 per building; small ground-clutter props skip the shadow pass (props are destructible multi-submesh GLBs, so MultiMesh batching isn't applicable — shadow-LOD is the safe equivalent); and idle weapon trails skip their per-frame `ImmediateMesh` rebuild. **New "Graphics Performance" settings group:** *Rendering Engine Quality* (High = Forward+, Low = Mobile renderer; persisted via an `override.cfg` next to the executable, applies on restart) and *Rendering Resolution* (High, or Upscaled = reduced internal 3D scale + FSR, applied live). **Projectile pooling was deliberately deferred** — its ~30 runtime-state fields have conditional-set hazards that would risk silent combat corruption; the pooling infra is ready for a focused follow-up. Verified: clean headless `--import` and all 11 `tools/test_*.tscn` regression suites pass; the GPU-particle / notifier-culling / FSR visuals still want an in-editor eyeball.
